text:
Gustav Forsling's overtime slap shot, a 5% chance by the numbers, beat Brandon Bussi at 4:55 and handed FLA a 1-0 win that CAR had spent most of the night earning the other way. The Hurricanes created 2.54 expected goals to FLA's 1.91, and in simulated replays of every shot they take this game 62% of the time.

Jacob Markstrom is the reason it never tilted. He stopped all 15 shots he faced, which were worth 2.54 expected goals, a swing of about two and a half goals in FLA's favor. CAR's best look came in the third period, when Jackson Blake had a 25% chance and missed the net. Even the power play brought no relief: CAR went 0 for 6 on chances worth 1.85 expected goals, while FLA was 0 for 7 on 0.59.

The strange part is that FLA actually controlled even strength, 1.29 expected goals to 0.52, and took 51 shot attempts to 37. CAR's edge came from the special teams minutes, where it made far better chances than it could convert. Forsling's goal was assisted by Carter Verhaeghe, whose line owned the ice at 0.64 expected goals for against 0.09. Forsling himself was on the ice for 1.75 expected goals against, and it still ended with his stick.
